requirement:
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.

HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes. Inline HTML comments
within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text. Paragraph and directive
prose uses word-based hashing. Reflowing whitespace within the same paragraph,
while preserving its words and surrounding outline structure, preserves the
hash. Changing its words changes the structural encoding.
rationale:
I judged this from the supplied test source only. I did not request any implementation source.

**Obligations derived from `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fingerprints`:**
1. The hash is SHA-256 over a structural encoding of whitespace-separated words.
2. The fingerprint scheme identifies the Markdown rules and their version. The scheme requirement is cited, not implemented here.
3. HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes.
4. Inline HTML comments inside paragraph text stay ordinary paragraph text, so they affect the hash.
5. Paragraph and directive prose use word-based hashing.
6. Reflowing whitespace within a paragraph, with the same words and surrounding structure, preserves the hash.
7. Changing the words changes the hash.

**Mapping to tests:**
- **SHA-256 form (1):** `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` in `tests/outline_content.rs` asserts that each Markdown fingerprint value is 64 characters long and all hex digits. It does not check the algorithm by name or against a known digest. A 64-hex-digit value is a reasonable check of the digest form.
- **Scheme (2):** `bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline` asserts that `Markdown` reports `fingerprint_scheme()` equal to `markdown-structural-v1`. It also asserts that the loaded `OutlineContent` retains that scheme.
- **Block comments excluded (3):**
  - `comments_are_excluded_from_hashes_in_every_other_profile` has a Markdown case. Changing the `<!-- note -->` text or removing the comment leaves the `section[H]` hash equal. Changing the prose word changes it.
  - `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` has a similar Markdown case.
  - `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` checks that only the block is recorded as a comment.
- **Inline comments are paragraph text (4):** The last assertion of `bundled_fingerprints_exclude_comments_and_preserve_word_boundaries` uses `text <!-- one --> prose`. It asserts that changing `one` to `two` inside the inline comment changes the section hash. `markdown_comments_are_html_comment_blocks_not_inline_comments` also asserts that the owner at that line is a `paragraph`, not a comment.
- **Word-based hashing and reflow (5, 6):**
  - `reflowing_markdown_paragraphs_keeps_the_hash` covers moving line breaks and joining lines. Both keep the hash.
  - `prose_words_are_encoded_separately` covers extra and leading or trailing whitespace. These keep the hash.
  - `markdown_hashes_include_paragraph_text_between_punctuation_tokens` covers multiple spaces. These keep the hash.
  - `anonymous_identities_survive_reflow_and_sibling_edits_and_number_duplicates` reflows a paragraph and a nested directive. It asserts that the hash and the selectors are unchanged.
  - `directive_prose_hashes_words_across_reflow_without_joining_them` covers directive prose, which is the directive-prose part of this obligation. It asserts that reflowing keeps the fingerprint and that joining words changes it.
- **Changed words change the hash (7):**
  - `ab cd` versus `abcd`, `brown fox` versus `brownfox`, and `ready.` versus `ready now.` all change the hash.
  - The anonymous-identities test asserts that a paragraph with different words has a different hash.
  - The directive test asserts that `two words` and `twowords` have different fingerprints.

**Gaps:** I found none. The tests cover each named mode: paragraph prose, directive prose, block comments, and inline comments. They cover both the preserve cases and the change cases, and the assertions are on hash equality or inequality. The tests carry {test} markings for this requirement.

text: :::{req} fingerprints
Structural hashes use SHA-256 over the unambiguous structural encoding and
whitespace-separated words under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`.
The fingerprint scheme identifies these rules and their version under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider.fingerprint_scheme`.
HTML comment blocks are excluded from structural hashes. Inline HTML comments
within paragraph text remain ordinary paragraph text. Paragraph and directive
prose uses word-based hashing. Reflowing whitespace within the same paragraph,
while preserving its words and surrounding outline structure, preserves the
hash. Changing its words changes the structural encoding.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
:::{req} language_provider.fingerprint_scheme
Each language supplies the scheme identifying its structural-hash rules and
their version. A change to those rules uses a different scheme; an update
preserving the calculation can retain the scheme. Loaded contents retain the
scheme used to compute their hashes.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Identify the structural-hash rules and their version.
fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
impl OutlineContent {
/// The selected item's structural digest from this snapshot.
pub fn structural_hash(&self) -> &str;
/// The retained scheme identifying its hashing rules and version.
pub fn fingerprint_scheme(&self) -> &str;
